### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /clip — 1cr

Returns detailed information about a specific Kick clip including the title, view count, duration, category, creator name, channel name, thumbnail URL, and creation timestamp.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Full URL of the Kick clip

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/kick/clip?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## What Kick is for

One endpoint, `/clip` (1cr): details for a single Kick clip.

There is no profile, no search and no channel listing — you need a clip URL or id to get
anything at all. That makes Kick a resolver, not a research surface: use it when a clip URL
turns up somewhere else and you need to know what it is.

For live-streaming research generally, `twitch` (4 endpoints, all 1cr) is the workable
platform.

## Field Maps


The `clip` endpoint returns a `Post` response normalized by the `kick-post` field map. Kick clip responses are nested under `clip.*` upstream; the field map flattens them. Includes computed fields under `data.computed`.
